text: The model has returned a "No Tumour" classification, which indicates that no features associated with the three tumour types it was trained on were identified, but it does not mean the scan is normal [neurasight-system]. This result is not a clean bill of health; the system only knows four categories and any other abnormality may be placed into the "No Tumour" class, and the absence of a detected tumour is not the same as the absence of disease [nci-cns-pdq-patient]. Because the conformal prediction set includes three or more classes, the output is inconclusive and must not be acted upon. Clinical correlation is required, and the finding should be reviewed by a qualified radiologist or specialist physician. If symptoms are present, matters a clinician may consider discussing include a clinical and neurological examination, formal radiological reporting of the full study, further or repeat imaging with appropriate sequences, investigation of non-tumour causes and specialist referral where symptoms persist or progress [nci-cns-pdq-patient] [ninds-brain-tumors].
